key_insight: PhysMiner combines triple-decomposition flow analysis with agentic LLM reasoning to automatically identify turbulence physics while reducing shear contamination.
engineering_relevance: The framework can support more reliable turbulence diagnostics and help derive improved subgrid-scale models for CFD and engineering flows.
method: Triple-decomposes the velocity-gradient tensor into rigid rotation, pure shear, and normal strain.
Uses agents to mine flow statistics, spatial structures, and literature knowledge for physical inference.
Adds a review agent and an evolving library to validate conclusions and reuse knowledge across cases.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation across five benchmarks and an end-to-end periodic hill study that produced an improved subgrid-scale model with better Reynolds-stress predictions.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of flow statistics and the robustness of agent reasoning, so cross-case generalization and physical validation remain important.
paper_title: PhysMiner: An Agentic AI Framework for Discovering Turbulence Physics
